title: Peak Performance
subtitle: Optimising skills without inventing deficits
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating peak performance within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain peak performance without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in peak performance.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to peak performance.

sections.explainSimply: Healthy performers may use neurofeedback to practise attention, calm or state control.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Performance outcomes are sensitive to expectancy, coaching, task familiarity and publication bias. Improvements should transfer to meaningful performance metrics.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Ethical practice avoids disease language, guarantees and opaque proprietary claims. Controlled evidence varies by sport and protocol.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Testing a treatment hypothesis: improvement must be meaningful, measured and compared with plausible alternatives.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand peak performance to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: A better training score may not transfer to the stage, field or exam.
sections.clinicalPearl: Measure benefit and harm with the same seriousness.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using peak performance predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: A better training score may not transfer to the stage, field or exam. Evidence classification: mixed and domain-specific evidence.

quizBank.question: What is the central clinical point of Peak Performance?
options: Healthy performers may use neurofeedback to practise attention, calm or state control.
Protocol choice requires no outcome measurement
Artifact is irrelevant once feedback begins
quizBank.explanation: Healthy performers may use neurofeedback to practise attention, calm or state control.

options: A better training score may not transfer to the stage, field or exam.

quizBank.question: How should the evidence for Peak Performance be communicated?
options: As mixed and domain-specific evidence, with methods and outcomes specified
As conclusively effective for all clients
By promising normalisation of the brain
quizBank.explanation: The appropriate evidence label is: mixed and domain-specific evidence.
